readThisFirst: This file defines what 'v6 works' means. Do not change a gate after seeing its result. To amend a gate, record a dated decision in PLAN.md and in this file BEFORE the locked holdout is used. See docs/dev/plans/city-cost-methodology-v6.md section 4.
whyTheseGatesDifferFromV5: v5 gated on per-relationship sample size (30 matched cities + 10 holdout per material relationship). That gate was unreachable from public sources -- eleven Expedia panels reached 18 and 26 matched cities and then flatlined -- and it was a proxy for an accuracy standard the fitted ladder already met at 11-13% leave-one-out error. v6 gates on what the product actually does: order cities correctly and get trip totals roughly right.

1_coverage.requirement: All 19 product fields numeric for at least 95% of in-scope cities, every value carrying an evidence grade
1_coverage.note: Grade D (regional prior) is permitted and expected for sparse cities. It must never be hidden or relabelled.

2_tierAccuracy.requirement: Per-tier held-out error against the ground-truth panel
2_tierAccuracy.note: v4 measured 18-22% as the realistic ceiling for this source class and the fitted ladder achieves 11-13%. 35% is a floor that admits the weak tiers (1-star, hostel split, activities), not a target. Report achieved figures per tier, never only the aggregate.

3_cityRanking.requirement: THE GATE THAT MATTERS. The product exists to answer 'Lisbon or Copenhagen?'
3_cityRanking.note: Ratios preserve ordering by construction, so this is more likely to pass than the tier gates. If it fails, the anchor measurement is the problem, not the ladder.

4_costBandAgreement.requirement: Assigned cost band matches the ground-truth band
4_costBandAgreement.note: v4 measured 63% exact agreement for newly generated cities, never off by more than one band. This must improve on that.

5_tripLevelRealism.requirement: Simulated 10-city trip total within tolerance of the ground-truth-composed total
5_tripLevelRealism.note: Independent per-city errors partially cancel across a trip. This is the number the user actually sees on the dashboard.

6_noRegressionVsV1.requirement: THE GATE v5 NEVER HAD. v6 must beat the shipping v1 dataset, which is the live alternative
6_noRegressionVsV1.note: v1 is 100% asserted with a refuted multiplier (accom_4_star = hotel_3star x 1.80, refuted at 38.8% median absolute error across 16 cities). Failing to beat it means v6 should not ship.

7_repeatability.requirement: Three independent calls on five deliberately difficult cities; report dispersion, never average it away
7_repeatability.note: Experiment 081 already measured 0% dispersion for the BudgetYourTrip activity route across three calls in four of five cities.

8_calibrationIntegrity.requirement: Every shipped source-calibration offset is fitted on enough cities and demonstrably helps
8_calibrationIntegrity.note: Prevents the source-offset mechanism becoming a new generation of asserted constants. An offset that does not clear this ships as 1.0 with the dispersion still widening the interval.

9_refreshEconomics.requirement: The real constraint from CLAUDE.md -- refresh must be cheap enough that it actually gets re-run
9_refreshEconomics.note: v5 constrained this to exactly 1 LLM call per city, which saved roughly A$10 per full refresh and forbade category specialisation, retry-on-block, and second samples. That was optimising a non-binding cost.

10_provenance.requirement: No grade C or D value renderable without its grade; blocked and not_found remain distinct
10_provenance.note: Inherited from v5 unchanged and non-negotiable. A modelled value must never be presentable as observed evidence.

groundTruthPanel.purpose: Fit all 19 product-tier derivations, fit source-calibration offsets, and score gates 2-6. The original six-measure panel was accommodation-scoped and made gates 2-6 only partly evaluable.
groundTruthPanel.collectionRule: MAY be collected by browser automation, manual research, or a stronger model. Ground truth is never in the production path, so it does not need to be target-model feasible. Food and drink ground truth MUST use independent official menus or venue price lists, never Numbeo; activity ground truth MUST use independent official operator or attraction pages, never BudgetYourTrip.

selectionRuleDefinitions.booking_top_picks_firstpage_median_v2: On the city-scoped Booking.com results page for the frozen window, use 2 adults / 1 room (1 adult for dorm), filter to the star class or Hostel, leave Booking's default Our top picks order, take every first-page listing meeting the class and occupancy spec, record all displayed public prices and use their median. Record the displayed class inventory count.
selectionRuleDefinitions.official_principal_museum_or_historic_si: Use the city's principal national or municipal museum or historic site. Record its standard adult general-admission tariff from the official operator page. Exclude theme parks, observation decks, zoos, aquariums and temporary or exhibition-specific pricing; if general admission is free, move to the next-ranked paid museum or historic site.
selectionRuleDefinitions.independent_street_food_panel_first5_med: Run a fixed city-scoped query for street food, market food, bakery takeaway and casual prepared meals. In search-result order, take the first five distinct eligible official vendor, market-board or tourism-listed venue pages that publish regular public prices for prepared savoury meals eaten out; from each page retain qualifying item prices in menu order until five prices are recorded, with no more than three prices from one page. Exclude drinks, desserts, packaged groceries, McDonald's or other global chains, delivery/aggregator prices, happy hours and temporary promotions. Record every selected single-person meal price and use the median; require at least three prices. If official city evidence establishes that no street-food category exists, record class_absent; otherwise an exhausted route is not_found.
selectionRuleDefinitions.independent_menu_panel_first5_median_v2: Run the fixed city-scoped query for the measure, take qualifying regular price observations from the first five distinct eligible official venue or operator menu pages in search-result order, stop at five observations, and use the median. Require at least three observations; if a qualifying menu supplies multiple comparable items, retain the first qualifying items in menu order until the panel has five observations. Exclude specials, happy hours, member prices, delivery prices, drinks from meal measures, and menus without a comparable serving basis. Inexpensive is one main for one at a casual/local venue; midrange is the lowest complete regular three-course meal for two at a midrange venue; premium is the lowest complete regular three-course or tasting-menu meal for two at a high-end venue; cappuccino, domestic draft beer and cocktail are one standard serving; wine is exactly the v5 volume-targeted 125-175 ml or 15 cl glass method from experiment 093.
selectionRuleDefinitions.official_mcdonalds_city_menu_first3_medi: Use official McDonald's local menu or restaurant pages found by the fixed city-scoped query, take the first three distinct city-specific pages in search-result order that display a standard Big Mac meal/combo price, record all three prices and use the median. If the official city menu exposes only one city-level price, record that one and mark the reduced sample in evidenceText.
selectionRuleDefinitions.official_operator_first3_halfday_group_m: Search the city for official operator pages, take the first three distinct eligible operators in search-result order selling a standard adult place on a scheduled group activity lasting approximately half a day, record the regular public adult price and use the median. Exclude private/custom tours, theme-park admission, observation decks, zoos, aquariums, and temporary promotions.
selectionRuleDefinitions.official_operator_first3_fullday_premium: Search the city for official operator pages, take the first three distinct eligible operators in search-result order selling a standard adult place on a scheduled full-day premium activity, record the regular public adult price and use the median. Exclude private/custom tours, theme-park admission, observation decks, zoos, aquariums, and temporary promotions.

requiredMetadata: dated one-night stay, two adults, one room (or one bed for dorm)
property name where the observation is property-level
all individual prices behind a panel median in samplePrices
selectionRule and the source-specific serving basis

lockedHoldout.lockRule: LOCKED per measure. Existing revealed_once measures are spent and must not be reread or rescored. New measures are sealed independently after collection, revealed once only after the all-19 candidate is frozen, and never used for tuning. If a new measure has been revealed, no coefficient, prompt, or gate may change.

stratification.note: The dataset's regions and bands do not fully cross -- there are no low-band European cities and no low-band North American or Oceania cities. The panel stratifies by region with band coverage where it exists rather than forcing an impossible full cross. Sparse cities are over-represented in the holdout on purpose: grade D behaviour must be characterised honestly, not averaged out of view.

expectedCallShape: A: Numbeo search snippets -> 5 food/drink anchors
B: Expedia 3-star class trend -> 1 accommodation level anchor
C: BudgetYourTrip entertainment tiers -> 3 activity anchors
D (optional): Expatistan -> cocktail and wine bottle; cross-check only unless independently validated
productionConstraint.retryRule: Retry is permitted on a 429/503 or a blocked page. A retry must be recorded. On repeated block, fail to the next grade -- never silently substitute a different source.
productionConstraint.directPageReadRationale: Experiment 015 returned HTTP 503 and 429 on canonical Numbeo URLs; Experiment 013 had all 15 official booking-engine URLs blocked at the web safety boundary. Search snippets only.

scoringRules.splitRule: Correlated observations from one city must never cross partitions.
reportRequirements: Per-tier figures, never only an aggregate
Per-region and per-band breakdown, so bias cannot hide inside an average
